summary.name: Presspeech
summary.one_liner: Presspeech is a local push-to-talk dictation app for Mac and Windows that transcribes speech on-device without an account or cloud transcription.
use_cases: dictate text into other apps by holding a key
voice typing on Apple Silicon Macs
summary.what_it_does: Presspeech lets you hold a key, speak, and release to dictate, or press a key to toggle recording. It transcribes speech locally with no account or cloud transcription. Missing speech models are downloaded on first launch, which may send a request to Hugging Face. Delivery into the destination app is automatic only when Presspeech can verify the destination window; otherwise it avoids automatic paste and may copy the transcript to the clipboard. The page lists a macOS 0.3.10 signed and notarised release for Apple Silicon on macOS 14+ and an unsigned Windows 0.1.12 x64 prerelease. It reports about 100 ms model transcription on benchmark clips, a 9.2 MB signed release zip, and about 80 MB RAM while idle.
notable: Fully local transcription with no account or cloud transcription
Verifies destination before automatic paste and falls back to clipboard notices
Listed under menubar apps in an open-source Mac apps collection
caveats: First launch with a missing speech model triggers a model download request; on some builds Setup cannot defer it, and the request may include a Hugging Face token or telemetry
Windows 0.1.12 is an unsigned prerelease; Windows 11 recommended
Clipboard and paste delivery can be unreliable; check the destination field before manually recovering a transcript
Specific builds carry launch-decision risks (proxy URL, telemetry, token); the page advises reading each version's launch decision before opening
